findings.name: brain MRI
findings.result: Bilateral T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in the temporal lobes and insular regions (worse on the left), extending into the corpus callosum, centrum semiovale, left basal ganglia, left thalamus, optic chiasm, and periventricular occipital white matter. The lesions are mildly expanded, with no diffusion restriction on DWI, no enhancement on postcontrast images, and no hemorrhagic foci on SWI.

findings.result: Increased retinal nerve fiber-layer thickness consistent with disc swelling.

aliases: diffuse glioma with a gliomatosis cerebri pattern
gold.reasoning: 1. Herpes simplex encephalitis — “HSE and LE were excluded based on incompatible clinical presentation, imaging findings, and laboratory data.” 2. Limbic encephalitis — “HSE and LE were excluded based on incompatible clinical presentation, imaging findings, and laboratory data.” 3. Infiltrative low-grade glioma — “Furthermore, due to volume expansion and facilitated diffusion of involved areas, we had to consider a differential diagnosis of neoplastic lesions such as infiltrative low-grade gliomas.” 4. Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy — “Lack of a previous history of immunodeficiency along with negative test result of HIV, absence of a typical pattern of enhancement and restriction seen in PML as well as the presence of mass effect and cortical involvement lessens the possibility of PML in our patient.” 5. Subacute sclerosing panencephalitis — “…but grey matter involvement and mass effect were not consistent with the diagnosis of SSPE.” 6. Toxic leukoencephalopathy, lymphomatosis cerebri, HIV encephalopathy, and PACNS — “We ruled out these differential diagnoses with laboratory results and lack of their specific imaging findings.”
